description: Number to string conversion and arithmetic edges. MoonSharp formats numbers with .NET's shortest round-trip text, not Lua 5.2's %.14g; notes give the Lua 5.2 result where it differs.

cases.name: tostring: small integers
cases.source: return { tostring(1), tostring(-1), tostring(0), tostring(100), tostring(2^31), tostring(3.0), tostring(-3.0) }

cases.name: tostring: integers up to 2^53 print every digit
cases.source: return { tostring(2^53), tostring(-2^53), tostring(1e15), tostring(1e16), tostring(123456789012345), tostring(2^53 + 2) }

cases.name: tostring: integers beyond 2^53 use exponent form
tostring: shortest round-trip fractions
cases.source: return { tostring(0.1 + 0.2), tostring(0.1), tostring(1/3), tostring(1.5), tostring(-2.25), tostring(1e15 + 0.5) }

cases.name: tostring: negative zero keeps its sign
math.huge is the largest double, not infinity
cases.note: Lua 5.2: inf, true, false. MoonSharp defines math.huge as Double.MaxValue

cases.name: string.format: integer conversions
cases.source: return { string.format('%d', 3), string.format('%05d', 42), string.format('%+d', 5), string.format('%-5d|', 5), string.format('%d', 2^31), string.format('%x', 255), string.format('%X', 255), string.format('%o', 8) }

cases.name: string.format: %d of 2^63 wraps
cases.note: Lua 5.2 raises bad argument #2 to 'format' (not a number in proper range)

cases.name: string.format: fixed and general
cases.source: return { string.format('%5.2f', 3.14159), string.format('%.3f', 2/3), string.format('%.14g', 0.1 + 0.2), string.format('%.17g', 0.1 + 0.2), string.format('%g', 1e20), string.format('%g', 0.0001) }

cases.name: tonumber: decimal forms
cases.source: return { tonumber('10'), tonumber('1e2'), tonumber(' 10 '), tonumber('1.5e1'), tonumber('.5'), tonumber('5.') }

cases.name: tonumber: invalid text is nil
cases.source: return { tonumber('') == nil, tonumber('abc') == nil, tonumber('1e') == nil, tonumber('0x') == nil, tonumber('inf') == nil }

cases.name: tonumber: nan and .NET number forms are nil
cases.source: return { tonumber('nan') == nil, tonumber('1,000') == nil, tonumber('(5)') == nil }

cases.name: modulo with a negative divisor takes the divisor's sign
floor, ceil, min, max
cases.source: return { math.floor(-3.5), math.ceil(-3.5), math.floor(2^53 + 0.5) == 2^53, math.max(1, 2.5, -1), math.min(3, 1/0), math.floor(7 / 2), math.floor(-7 / 2) }

cases.name: NaN comparisons are all false
cases.source: local n = 0/0 return { n ~= n, n < 1, n > 1, n >= 1, n <= 1 }

cases.name: number keys: 1 and 1.0 are one key
string coercion rejects what Lua does not read

expectError.messageContains: attempt to perform arithmetic on a string value

cases.name: exponent followed by + needs spaces
cases.note: Lua 5.2 reads 1e15 + 0.5; the MoonSharp lexer takes the + into the number
